verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. Reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC swaps A and C and sends D to E, so it preserves the multiset of side lengths and the relevant opposite-angle sum; the complementary opposite-angle sum is then also preserved. For fixed cyclic side lengths and a fixed sum of the angles at B and D, the law-of-cosines equation has at most one admissible angle at B because its two sides are respectively strictly increasing and strictly decreasing. The resulting two triangles have a unique convex gluing up to isometry, establishing the uniqueness lemma. Finally, each of twenty-five consecutive quadrilaterals can be assigned one of at most 24 ordered side-length quadruples with the same chosen opposite-angle sum, so the pigeonhole principle and the uniqueness lemma force two to be congruent. There are no external references, cited fact IDs, hard-prohibition violations, critical errors, or gaps.
